plan: Given my private value of $6, I should avoid overbidding to prevent losses. Rational bidders will likely bid close to their value, aiming to win only if profitable. I should bid slightly less than my value, say $5, to avoid paying more than the prize is worth to me and to ensure potential profit if I win. This strategy limits risk and maximizes potential profit.

Given my value of $40, I should bid slightly below it to maximize profit if I win, while still having a high chance of winning. Rational bidders will likely bid close to their values, which are uniformly distributed between $0 and $49. Bidding slightly below my value, around $38, balances the risk of losing with the potential profit margin if I win. This strategy considers that other bidders are also trying to maximize their earnings and might bid close to their values.

Given my value of $28, I aim to bid just below my value to maximize profit if I win. Assuming rational behavior, Andy and Betty will bid close to their values. To win, I should bid slightly above the expected average bid of $24.5 (midpoint of $0-$49). Hence, I will bid $25. This maximizes my chance of winning while ensuring potential profit ($28 value - $25 bid = $3 profit) if the second-highest bid is lower.
